title: Two versions side by side
description:
A library sometimes has to change what a function does while old code still needs the old behaviour. An **inline namespace** handles that: its contents are visible as if they were in the enclosing namespace, so it marks the *current* version.

Right now `geometry::area` uses a rough value of pi. Reorganise it:

- Move the existing function, unchanged, into `namespace v1` inside `geometry`.
- Add an `inline namespace v2` inside `geometry` with an `area` that uses `std::numbers::pi`.

Afterwards `geometry::area(r)` means the new one, and anyone who needs the old result can still ask for `geometry::v1::area(r)`.
unitTests:
TEST("the plain name means the current version") { CHECK_NEAR(geometry::area(1.0), 3.141592653589793, 1e-12); CHECK_NEAR(geometry::area(2.0), 12.566370614359172, 1e-12); }
TEST("both versions can still be named") { CHECK_NEAR(geometry::v1::area(1.0), 3.14, 1e-12); CHECK_NEAR(geometry::v2::area(1.0), 3.141592653589793, 1e-12); CHECK_NEAR(geometry::v1::area(10.0), 314.0, 1e-9); }
lessonTitle: Name Lookup, ADL, Inline Namespaces and the ODR
